# A STRESS DOMAIN, NOT AN EXAMPLE — lives under qa/stress_domains/, not
# examples/, on purpose (see qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook's own
# "being clever" note and .claude/skills/hecks_qa/SKILL.md's "Authoring a
# new stress domain" section).
#
# THE CONSTRUCT-COMBINATION THIS DOMAIN IS FOR, ABSENT FROM THE ENTIRE
# CORPUS UNTIL NOW: a `process_manager` (saga) whose own `dispatch` leg
# targets a command owned by a NESTED ENTITY, not a plain aggregate.
# Every `process_manager` in this repository — banking's own
# `Onboarding`/`Settlement`/`ExternalSettlement`, quality_control's own
# `BugCiWatch` — dispatches exclusively into AGGREGATE-level commands.
# `qa/stress_domains/nested_pieces` proved a two-level nested entity
# fuzzes and dispatches correctly through ORDINARY (non-saga) addressing.
# Neither combination — saga leg targeting an entity command — had ever
# been declared anywhere, checked directly against every existing
# `process_manager` in the corpus (`grep -rn 'dispatch ' examples/
# banking/bluebook/*.bluebook qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook`)
# before this domain was authored.
#
# WHAT THIS DOMAIN FOUND, FIRST TRY — BUG#6, NOW FIXED: the combination
# did not work, in two compounding ways, both in shared runtime dispatch
# code this domain's own bluebook never needed to change:
#
#   1. `SagaInterpreter#qualified` (`lib/hecks/runtime/saga_interpreter.
#      rb`) used to decide whether a dispatch's own `command_name`
#      already carried an explicit domain qualifier with one heuristic:
#      `command_name.include?("::")`. That heuristic could not tell a
#      genuinely cross-domain reference (`Banking::Account::Debit` — one
#      `::` survives `Naming.command_ref`'s own rewrite) apart from a
#      bare, SAME-DOMAIN entity command reference (`Manifest::Slot::
#      Fill` — ALSO one `::` survives, for an unrelated reason: entity
#      nesting, not a domain qualifier), and picked the cross-domain
#      reading unconditionally — so `Manifest::Slot::Fill` dispatched
#      unprefixed, and `Naming.split_verb` read "Manifest" as a domain
#      name instead of this chapter's own aggregate. Fixed by dropping
#      the guess entirely: confirmed against the whole corpus, no saga
#      anywhere ever dispatches genuinely cross-domain, so a saga
#      dispatch is now always qualified against its own home domain,
#      unconditionally — the same default `PolicyInterpreter#deliver`
#      already applied via its own explicit (never string-inferred)
#      `target_domain` field.
#
#   2. Once (1) resolved the verb correctly, `ReactionInvocation.build`
#      (`lib/hecks/runtime/reaction_invocation.rb`) still could not
#      resolve the manifest's own receiver identity: `source_receiver_
#      for` refused outright whenever a target carried any entities, and
#      separately misread `target.command.creates?` — true for EVERY
#      entity command by construction, not only a genuinely creating one
#      — as a reason to refuse inheriting the aggregate's own identity
#      from the triggering event. Both were dead code paths (no policy
#      or saga anywhere had ever targeted an entity command while
#      relying on an inherited receiver) until this domain exercised
#      them for the first time. Fixed to match `build`'s own already-
#      correct `target.entities.empty? && target.command.creates?` guard
#      one caller below.
#
# See `saga_interpreter.rb`'s `qualified` and `reaction_invocation.rb`'s
# `source_receiver_for` for the full fix and reasoning; `NOTES.md` still
# carries the original reproduction write-up for the historical record.
#
# THE DOMAIN ITSELF models a small warehouse consignment: a `Consignment`
# request starts a `Packing` saga, which opens a `Manifest`, reserves a
# numbered `Slot` on it (an aggregate-level dispatch), then fills that
# slot (`Manifest::Slot::Fill`, an ENTITY-level dispatch — the leg BUG#6
# broke) with a `compensates Manifest::Slot::Clear` alongside it
# (per-dispatch saga compensation targeting an entity command for the
# first time anywhere in this corpus too). The saga's own `:refused` leg
# cancels the consignment — now reachable only on a genuine refusal, not
# structurally on every run: `ConsignmentShipped` (this process
# manager's own `ends_on`) is the ordinary happy path, and `spec/
# waybill_spec.rb` pins exactly that end-to-end.
Hecks.bluebook "Waybill" do
  vision "A consignment saga that opens a manifest, reserves a slot on it, and tries to fill that slot through the saga's own dispatch — the first process manager anywhere in this corpus to target a nested entity's own command, rather than a plain aggregate's."

  core

  aggregate "Consignment" do
    description "A request to pack and ship one item, driving the Packing saga end to end."

    attribute :reference, ConsignmentReference
    identified_by :reference

    attribute :number, SlotNumber
    attribute :item,   ItemLabel

    value_object "ConsignmentReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a consignment is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # SAME SHAPE AS `nested_pieces`' OWN `BoardNumber`/`CardSequence` —
    # positive-only, so `0` is non-blank (survives routing) and still
    # fails the invariant once a typed rebuild is attempted. Declared
    # again here (Manifest declares its own copy too, below) rather than
    # shared — this corpus's own convention (`Transfer`'s aliased
    # `reference_to Account, as: :source`/`:destination` aside, no
    # existing chapter shares one value object BY NAME across two
    # aggregates without redeclaring it locally; `bluebook_builder/
    # validation.rb`'s own `correlates_by` check reads each owning
    # aggregate's OWN `value_object` table, never a cross-aggregate one).
    value_object "SlotNumber" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a slot number is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "ItemLabel" do
      attribute :text, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("an item is labeled") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    lifecycle :status, default: "requested" do
      transition "Ship"   => "shipped",   from: "requested"
      transition "Cancel" => "cancelled", from: "requested"
    end

    command "Request" do
      role "Customer"
      goal "Request one item be packed onto a numbered slot and shipped"

      attribute :reference, ConsignmentReference
      attribute :number,    SlotNumber
      attribute :item,      ItemLabel

      emits ConsignmentRequested
    end

    command "Ship", from: "requested" do
      role "System"
      goal "Mark the consignment shipped once its slot is filled"

      reference_to Consignment

      emits ConsignmentShipped
    end

    command "Cancel", from: "requested" do
      role "System"
      goal "Cancel a consignment whose slot could not be filled"

      reference_to Consignment

      emits ConsignmentCancelled
    end

    query "Requested" do
      description "Consignments still awaiting a packed, shipped slot."
      where(status: "requested")
      order_by :reference
    end
  end

  aggregate "Manifest" do
    description "One manifest, holding numbered slots the Packing saga fills one at a time."

    identified_by :reference

    attribute :reference, ManifestReference
    attribute :slots,     list_of(Slot)

    value_object "ManifestReference" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a manifest is referenced") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "SlotNumber" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a slot number is positive") { value.positive? }
    end

    value_object "ItemLabel" do
      attribute :text, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("an item is labeled") { !text.to_s.empty? }
    end

    command "Open" do
      role "Loader"
      goal "Open a manifest for a consignment"

      attribute :reference, ManifestReference

      emits ManifestOpened
    end

    command "AddSlot" do
      role "Loader"
      goal "Reserve a numbered slot on the manifest"

      reference_to Manifest
      attribute :number, SlotNumber

      sets :slots, append: { number: :number }

      emits SlotAdded
    end

    # S17, ADR 0026 — a piece nested inside a piece, one level (see
    # `qa/stress_domains/nested_pieces` for two). THE WHOLE REASON THIS
    # DOMAIN EXISTS: a `process_manager`'s own `dispatch` targeting
    # `Fill`, below, is the untested combination — see this file's own
    # header comment for the exact gap it surfaces.
    entity "Slot" do
      description "One numbered slot on the manifest, filled with one item."

      identified_by :number

      attribute :number, SlotNumber
      attribute :item,   ItemLabel, optional: true

      command "Fill" do
        role "Loader"
        goal "Load an item into the slot"

        attribute :item, ItemLabel

        sets :item

        emits SlotFilled
      end

      # THE COMPENSATING HALF OF `Fill` — armed for the saga's own leg 3
      # (`Manifest::Slot::Fill`), which now delivers (see this file's own
      # header comment: BUG#6, fixed). `compensates` targeting an ENTITY
      # command is, itself, a second combination absent from the rest of
      # the corpus (banking's own `Settlement` compensates
      # `Account::Credit`, a plain aggregate command) — this domain is
      # its regression pin too, exercised whenever leg 3 genuinely
      # refuses.
      command "Clear" do
        role "Loader"
        goal "Clear a slot's item back out — the compensating half of Fill"

        attribute :item, ItemLabel

        sets :item

        emits SlotCleared
      end
    end
  end

  # THE SAGA ITSELF. `correlates_by :"reference.value"` — the SAME
  # dotted field name on both `Consignment` (the starting aggregate) and
  # every dispatch target below, matching every existing corpus saga's
  # own convention (Onboarding/Settlement/ExternalSettlement/BugCiWatch
  # all correlate on one dotted scalar shared across every aggregate a
  # leg touches).
  process_manager "Packing" do
    correlates_by :"reference.value"
    starts_on Consignment::ConsignmentRequested
    ends_on   Consignment::ConsignmentShipped

    # LEG 1 — AGGREGATE-LEVEL, WORKS TODAY. Fires on the saga's own
    # starting event, the same self-transition-on-starts_on shape
    # `Settlement`'s own first leg and `BugCiWatch` both already use.
    transition Consignment::ConsignmentRequested => "packing", from: "packing" do
      dispatch Manifest::Open, with: { reference: :reference }
    end

    # LEG 2 — AGGREGATE-LEVEL, WORKS TODAY.
    transition Manifest::ManifestOpened => "packing", from: "packing" do
      dispatch Manifest::AddSlot, with: { reference: :reference, number: :number }
    end

    # LEG 3 — THE ENTITY-LEVEL DISPATCH THIS DOMAIN EXISTS TO EXERCISE.
    # See this file's own header comment: this used to refuse every
    # time, structurally (BUG#6, now fixed) — `Manifest::Slot::Fill`
    # delivers correctly today.
    transition Manifest::SlotAdded => "filling", from: "packing" do
      dispatch Manifest::Slot::Fill, with: { number: :number, item: :item } do
        compensates Manifest::Slot::Clear, with: { number: :number, item: :item }
      end
    end

    # THE HAPPY-PATH LEG — reachable now that leg 3 above delivers;
    # `spec/waybill_spec.rb` pins this exact end-to-end run.
    transition Manifest::SlotFilled => "filled", from: "filling" do
      dispatch Consignment::Ship, with: { reference: :reference }
    end

    # THE COMPENSATING LEG — fires on a genuine refusal of leg 3, not
    # structurally on every run (see header comment: that was BUG#6).
    transition :refused => "cancelled", from: "filling" do
      dispatch Consignment::Cancel, with: { reference: :reference }
    end
  end
end
